description.value: The study investigated the relation between trait impulsivity and cortical morphometry in cocaine users and non-drug using controls using surface-based morphometry.

spans.text: The current study was designed to investigate the distinct relation between trait impulsivity, as measured by the BIS-11, and cortical morphometry in cocaine users and non-drug using controls by means of SBM.

description.value: Cross-sectional comparison of regular cocaine users and non-drug using controls.

definition.value: Main effect of group on surface area across the predefined cortical regions of interest.

spans.text: In contrast to previous studies we did not find differences in CV between cocaine users and controls ( ).

value: The MANCOVA on SA indicated that there was a main effect of group across all ROIs.
Cocaine users had a smaller SA of the superior temporal cortex but a larger SA of the insula compared to controls.

model_representation_notes.value: Multivariate ANCOVA adjusted for age and intracranial volume; post-hoc ANCOVAs were corrected for multiple comparisons.

name.value: group by impulsivity interaction on cortical surface area

definition.value: Group by impulsivity interaction on surface area across the predefined cortical regions of interest.

value: The MANCOVA on SA indicated that there was a main effect of group and a group by impulsivity interaction across all ROIs.
There were divergent relations between trait impulsivity and SA of the superior temporal cortex and insula: positive in controls and negative in cocaine users.

model_representation_notes.value: Multivariate ANCOVA adjusted for age and intracranial volume; significant interactions were followed by partial correlations adjusted for age and intracranial volume.

name.value: monthly cocaine use and cortical thickness

definition.value: Association between monthly cocaine use and cortical thickness within cocaine users.

value: Within cocaine users, monthly cocaine use was the only significant predictor of cortical thickness.
Monthly cocaine use was negatively associated with cortical thickness of the superior temporal cortex and insula; the association with the insula did not survive multiple-comparisons correction.

model_representation_notes.value: Multivariate ANCOVA adjusted for age and intracranial volume; follow-up tests were corrected for multiple comparisons.

Images were acquired on a 3.0-T whole body MR scanner (Philips Achieva) with a 32 channel SENSE head coil.
